Use parameters and returns to separate game rules

Unit 1 · Week 5 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Before class verify the nominated editor uses a school-approved Python/Pygame installation. Extract the whole pygame-teaching-pack.zip into a writable disposable folder. Open https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2 and workbook.md, faded_practice.py, practice-tests.csv and readiness.csv. Run python lab_runner.py 2. Use supplied named state/runner infrastructure; no student-authored classes, paid media or assessed project code. Record device, interpreter and support. Paper traces support reasoning; live window/keyboard evidence remains necessary. The suggested 55-minute allocation is untrialled; use the supplied 50-minute adaptation when required.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Open the matching Pygame lab · Practice workbook · Test record · Readiness record

1. Functions separate the game rules

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Run python lab_runner.py 2. This stage has movement and an active timer, with no station scoring. Success: explain new_state, command and update, restore reset values and show that a paused update changes neither x nor remaining time. Read state["mode"] as a supplied named slot. Dictionary infrastructure is provided; authoring dictionaries/classes is not a new Year 11 assessment requirement. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

2. Retrieve a call and its result

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and partner explanation

Give silent thinking time. w and h are parameters; 7 and 2 are arguments; return w*h gives 14 to the caller. print displays text and a function without an explicit return value returns None on normal completion. Use one brief foundation trace, then transfer to the supplied lab functions. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

3. One function returns a fresh state

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher think-aloud and call trace

Excerpt from lab_rules.new_state. Run the supplied stage before tracing. The caller receives a state store; field meanings are mode, horizontal position, active milliseconds, score, active station flags and whether a result was saved. Values are supplied infrastructure. Calling new_state twice creates separate dictionaries/lists. Show that changing a local scalar name does not rebind the caller variable, whereas updating a shared state slot is deliberately visible to the caller. Keep the distinction concrete rather than adding dictionary theory. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

4. Trace the start, pause and reset rules

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided state trace with faded support

Run stage 2 using Space to start/pause/resume and R to reset. command(state, action) receives a supplied mutable state and deliberately changes it; its normal return value is None. The runner processes transitions before update and discards the delta on a start/resume/reset frame, so paused wall time is not charged on resuming. Reset restores x=308, 20000 ms, score 0, fresh active flags and saved=False. Teacher models ready→playing; pairs predict later rows. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

5. A function can change its argument

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, investigate and explain

Call rules.update(state,1,250,collect=False) from a playing interior state: x 308→358, remaining 20000→19750. With mode paused, the same call changes neither value. new_state returns a value; update deliberately mutates its argument and returns None. Its direction, dt_ms and collect parameters receive 1,250,False here. Assigning x=999 to an unrelated local name has no effect on state["x"]. Drawing reads state but must not call update. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

6. Complete the changed state transitions

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent faded task and test record

Use a COPY of faded_practice.py. Changed initial values are x=40, remaining=15000, active=[True,True,True], score=0 and saved=False. Complete Space transitions and reset using new_state; keep the runner and collision/file code supplied or temporarily out of scope. For movement-only practice, complete only the paused/ready/finished guard and bounded movement/timer part of update with collect=False. Keep stations and persistence for later lessons. Make a fresh state per test. A paused 95000 ms update must leave position and remaining unchanged. For playing x=40, direction1,250 ms at speed160 gives x80 and14750 ms. Do not import the worked solution into the independent rules file. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

7. Does a local name explain mutation?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student misconception check

B. Local parameter names refer to objects; deliberately changing shared contents is visible. Rebinding a local parameter to a new object is different. Use an actual reset trace, not an assertion that every function changes globals. If learners choose A, compare one local scalar assignment with state["mode"]="paused". Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-2; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

8. Explain a return and a reset

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit explanation

Use two fresh states: mutate one active flag and show the other still True; after reset, the changed version restores all three flags. Ask for a new unseen action sequence without the reference open. Record expected/actual and support in y11-2 workbook/readiness. Missing evidence means reteach before project issue. No claim of classroom completion is made by this suggested timing.
